title: Aldosterone

questions.q: What is aldosterone?
questions.answer: Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid hormone, a steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.

questions.q: Where is aldosterone produced?
questions.answer: Aldosterone is produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.

triples.o: zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland

questions.q: What is the function of aldosterone?
questions.answer: Aldosterone is essential for sodium conservation in the kidney, salivary glands, sweat glands and colon, and plays a central role in the homeostatic regulation of blood pressure, plasma sodium, and potassium levels.

triples.o: sodium conservation in the kidney, salivary glands, sweat glands and colon
homeostatic regulation of blood pressure, plasma sodium (Na), and potassium (K) levels

questions.q: How does aldosterone act?
questions.answer: Aldosterone acts mainly on the mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal tubules and collecting ducts of the nephron.

triples.o: mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal tubules and collecting ducts of the nephron

questions.q: What does aldosterone influence in the kidney?
questions.answer: Aldosterone influences the reabsorption of sodium and excretion of potassium of the kidney, thereby indirectly influencing water retention or loss, blood pressure and blood volume.

triples.o: reabsorption of sodium and excretion of potassium of the kidney
water retention or loss, blood pressure and blood volume

questions.q: What happens when aldosterone is dysregulated?
questions.answer: When dysregulated, aldosterone is pathogenic and contributes to the development and progression of cardiovascular and renal disease.

triples.o: development and progression of cardiovascular and renal disease when dysregulated

questions.q: What is the iron response element?
questions.answer: The iron response element (IRE) is a short conserved stem-loop which is bound by iron response proteins (IRPs, also named IRE-BP or IRBP).

questions.q: What binds the iron response element?
questions.answer: Iron response proteins (IRPs, also named IRE-BP or IRBP) bind the IRE.

questions.q: Where is the iron response element found?
questions.answer: The IRE is found in UTRs (untranslated regions) of various mRNAs whose products are involved in iron metabolism.

triples.o: untranslated regions of mRNAs involved in iron metabolism

questions.q: Which mRNA contains one IRE in its 5' UTR?
questions.answer: The mRNA of ferritin (an iron storage protein) contains one IRE in its 5' UTR.

questions.q: What happens when iron concentration is low and IRPs bind the IRE in ferritin mRNA?
questions.answer: When iron concentration is low, IRPs bind the IRE in the ferritin mRNA and cause reduced translation rates.

triples.s: IRP binding to IRE in ferritin mRNA under low iron

questions.q: What is the effect of IRP binding to multiple IREs in the 3' UTR of the transferrin receptor mRNA?
questions.answer: Binding to multiple IREs in the 3' UTR of the transferrin receptor (involved in iron acquisition) leads to increased mRNA stability.

questions.answer: United States law distinguishes what it calls treaties from executive agreement, congressional-executive agreements, and sole executive agreements.

questions.q: What is the status of treaties, executive agreements, congressional-executive agreements, and sole executive agreements under international law?
questions.answer: All four classes are equally treaties under international law; they are distinct only from the perspective of internal American law.

questions.q: What primarily distinguishes treaties from other classes of agreements in United States law?
questions.answer: The distinctions are primarily concerning their method of approval.

questions.answer: Congressional-executive agreements require majority approval by both the House and the Senate, either before or after the treaty is signed by the President.

questions.q: Who may execute sole executive agreements?
questions.answer: Sole executive agreements may be executed by the President acting alone.
